fullDescription: A single ANIMATED WEBGL SHADER: Dot Orbit, a rigid lattice where every dot has its own phase. The coordinate is floored to a lattice and a phase is hashed per cell, so each dot orbits its own cell centre while the lattice itself never moves. It is a full-bleed fragment shader with no page around it, about 4KB, no textures, no images and no animation library, and it reacts to the pointer. Drop it behind a hero, a section or a whole page as a living background. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one static frame, and it falls back cleanly where WebGL is absent.

structured.summary: A full-viewport animated WebGL fragment shader called Dot Orbit: a rigid lattice where every dot has its own phase. The coordinate is floored to a lattice and a phase is hashed per cell, so each dot orbits its own cell centre while the lattice itself never moves. The page contains nothing but the canvas. A shared GLSL preamble provides a hashed value noise, a six-octave fbm and a two-level domain-warp helper; this effect draws on them and adds its own body. Pointer movement raises a smoothed intensity uniform so the effect strengthens under the cursor and relaxes when it leaves.

style.description: Generative light on a committed ground. Every colour is computed per pixel from a clock and a coordinate; nothing is sampled from an image.
style.prompt: Ground #080501 with accents ["#FF9E29", "#2B1400"]. There is no typography and no page chrome: the shader is the entire surface. Keep the palette to two or three values so the effect reads as one material rather than a rainbow.

layout_and_structure.description: A single full-viewport canvas, fixed to the viewport, with a hidden fallback panel behind it.

prompts.prompt: One canvas fixed at inset 0 filling the viewport, with html and body at 100 percent height, margin 0 and overflow hidden. Behind it a hidden panel that is only shown when no WebGL context can be created.
